newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat licences from July held at zero Ecu.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat licences from July held at zero Ecu.

text.p: European Union wheat export licences issued since March will not be cut below zero Ecus per tonne in July or August, an EU grain official confirmed Thursday.
The EU usually penalises export licences issued near the end of one July/June export campaign so that they cannot be used for new-crop wheat available from July.

It uses the so-called negative corrective system to reduce the export refund to non-profitable levels from July onwards. But since refunds have now reached zero after falling in recent weeks, they cannot be cut any further, the official said.
"All refunds given out since March will be worth zero after July," the official said. "You can't go to less than zero."
Export licences are valid for the current month plus four months, so that licences issued in March are valid until the end of July. Those issued this month are valid until the end of August.

The unusual pattern this year means traders can hold on to recently awarded licences for early sales of the next crop at a zero refund, even though they were issued during the previous July/June campaign.
